markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **jointly learned title/description fusion within the corrected GRU4Rec**. This is an untested proposal; the supplied inspiration’s 0.5687 score is historical evidence, not a result for this idea.

Three starting insights guide the experiment. First, scalar retention can suppress stale interests, but cannot directly enrich item identity; additional representation learning addresses a complementary limitation. Second, Electronics has 9.7% sampled ranking errors and a 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin, motivating better discrimination. Third, mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 imply approximately orthogonal embeddings, giving no justification for a collapse penalty.

Three literature insights narrow the design. CLA-Rec and ITS-Rec motivate text–interaction alignment, although their pretrained encoders and other inputs exceed this task’s constraints. Official GRU4Rec supports BPR-max as an objective-level intervention. Hard-BPR cautions that difficult unobserved items can be false negatives, supporting separation of representation changes from mining changes.

The framework separates **representation**, **objective**, and **memory** interventions. Evaluate three alternatives below. O/P/U/M/D denote originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each assessment includes a supporting (+) and limiting (−) reason.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ID–text fusion [1,2] | 3: +constraint-compatible adaptation; −established fusion | 7: +transferable representation; −sparse text | 7: +specific item connections; −no compatibility guarantee | 7: +richer discrimination; −unmeasured margins | 4: +pooled encoder; −scoring integration |
| Uniform-pool BPR-max [3,4] | 2: +targeted application; −established loss | 6: +direct ranking signal; −sampling sensitivity | 4: +stronger ordering; −no richer identity | 8: +emphasizes confusing negatives; −false negatives | 3: +localized loss change; −pooling cost |
| Fast/slow GRU state [5] | 4: +task-specific adaptation; −existing temporal memory | 7: +changing interests; −identifiability | 7: +recent versus old interests; −limited item semantics | 6: +context discrimination; −indirect evidence | 7: +single network; −recurrence and serialization changes |

Select fusion because it explicitly targets two user failures: broadly related products lacking a specific purpose connection, and media lacking an identifiable artist/story/style connection. It also targets Electronics’ weak positive–negative separation. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated semantic understanding.

Encode available titles/descriptions using randomly initialized token embeddings and masked mean pooling. Fuse the projected text vector with the ID vector using a learned scalar gate; use that same representation for GRU inputs and candidate scoring. Preserve the baseline loss, sampler and schedule initially, isolating representation changes.

```python
text = masked_mean(token_embedding(tokens), token_mask)
gate = sigmoid(gate_layer(concat(id_vector, text)))
item = id_vector + gate * project(text)
features = corrected_gru(item_history)
score = dot(final_nonpadding_feature(features), candidate_item)
```

Initialize the gate near 0.1; missing text contributes zero. Retain all four routes, one checkpoint/category, seeds 0/42, ≤200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, and the pinned macro HR@10 selection. Update predictor serialization and preserve diagnostic interfaces. Report unavailable category attributes as unavailable. No experiments were executed.

References correspond to the linked works below.

idea.description: Add a lightweight title/description encoder trained from scratch to the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. Jointly learn a gated residual text contribution to each item-ID representation, using the identical fused representation for observed-history inputs and candidate scoring. Train one network and deploy one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broadly related products without a concrete purpose connection and media without identifiable connections to preferred artists, stories or sounds. Available text may provide more specific item evidence than IDs alone. Electronics’ 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate and 0.0265 lower-tail margin motivate testing whether this evidence improves discrimination. Text cannot establish equipment compatibility, ownership redundancy or current mood reliably; improvements require measurement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Implement against the supplied corrected baseline; its source and resolved configuration were not included here. Preserve its GRU architecture, dimensions, optimizer, objective, sampling and checkpoint schedule for the first comparison. Build deterministic token indices from allowed titles/descriptions without downloading weights or consulting held-out interactions. Use a bounded vocabulary or deterministic hashing, reserve padding, cap text length, and cache token indices rather than detached training-time embeddings. Initialize token embeddings randomly; apply a masked mean and a projection into the existing item embedding dimension. Fuse as e_i = v_i + sigmoid(w^T[v_i;t_i]+b) P(t_i), with zero gate weights and b approximately -2.197. Set the text contribution to zero for missing text and the complete representation to zero for item padding. Gate initialization is a hypothesis, not exact baseline equivalence.

Ensure the host item_emb interface exposes the effective representation consistently wherever diagnostics or scoring use it; preserve required attributes from the actual ModelView implementation. Preserve log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and the actual trained module at view.model. Freeze recurrent states on padding and read the maximum nonpadding index, handling empty histories explicitly. Keep causal next-item inputs unchanged.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, the supplied splits and evaluator, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Write artifacts under the trial directory. Each category loads exactly one jointly trained network/checkpoint. Do not add independent text, popularity or transition predictors. Cache effective item vectors only in evaluation mode after loading the selected checkpoint, invalidating caches whenever weights change.

Update the embedded predictor writer with the same text vocabulary or hashing configuration, token arrays, architecture, scoring and state-dict layout. Verify freshly loaded predictor scores against the selected in-memory model on identical histories and candidates. Bound profiling and diagnostic cost within the shared GPU budget. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Measure valid-position margins using the effective representations; unavailable category attributes must remain unavailable. Do not infer collapse from mapped cosine values near 0.5.

Compare against the corrected baseline using only pinned macro validation HR@10. Track per-category effects and the existing margin diagnostics as secondary evidence. Keep BPR-max and temporal-memory alternatives for separate trials; do not combine modifications before attributing the fusion effect. No performance improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class TextItemRepresentation(nn.Module):
    # Match dimensions and interface to the supplied baseline.
    def forward(item_ids):
        ids = id_embedding(item_ids)
        tokens, mask = token_table[item_ids], token_mask[item_ids]
        text = masked_mean(token_embedding(tokens), mask)
        alpha = sigmoid(gate(concat(ids, text)))
        fused = ids + alpha * text_projection(text) * has_text[item_ids]
        return fused * (item_ids != 0)[..., None]

# Train all parameters jointly; there is no separately fitted text model.
for category in supplied_four_categories:
    seed_training(42)
    model = corrected_GRU4Rec(item_representation=TextItemRepresentation(config))
    for epoch in range(min(host_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            batch = unchanged_family_sample_batch()
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(model, batch)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_text_configuration(category)

# Predictor uses the same effective item representation and scoring head.
features = model.log2feats(left_padded_history)
last = max_index_where(left_padded_history != 0)  # never count - 1
scores = baseline_empty_handling_or_predict_score(features, last, candidates)
write_matching_embedded_predictor()
verify_loaded_predictor_score_parity()

# Preserve DiagnosisProbe and interpreter signatures.
# Diagnose only measured margins/embeddings and available public fields.

originality.positive: A constrained adaptation combines a scratch-trained text encoder, shared input/output representations and the corrected GRU backbone in one network.
originality.negative: Text–ID fusion and joint representation learning are established; the supplied search results do not establish novelty.

future_potential.positive: An isolated representation experiment can establish whether permitted item text helps specific matching across both product and media domains.
future_potential.negative: Short or generic descriptions may add noise, and gains under sampled validation may not transfer to full-catalog user utility.

code_difficulty.positive: Masked pooling and a scalar gate are small additions that preserve fused GRU execution and require no pretrained assets.
code_difficulty.negative: Consistent item representations, metadata serialization, evaluation caching and ModelView compatibility require careful integration.

related_work.title: [1] CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes alignment between description embeddings and collaborative information, motivating recommendation-specific text representations.
limitations: Its LLM-derived embeddings and Transformer architecture do not satisfy this experiment’s constraints.
It does not establish gains for scratch-trained text fusion in GRU4Rec.

related_work.title: [2] ITS-Rec (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary describes encoding textual item information for recommendation.
limitations: Its BERT encoder and review inputs cannot be transferred to this task.
Only permitted titles and descriptions may inform the proposed adaptation.

related_work.title: [3] Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides established cross-entropy and BPR-max objectives for recurrent recommendation.
limitations: Objective recommendations do not demonstrate improvement on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [4] Hard-BPR (2024)
contributions: Addresses false-negative effects in hard-negative learning for implicit recommendation.
limitations: Its setting does not establish efficacy for this sequential GRU4Rec task.

related_work.title: [5] LSARN (2023 preprint)
contributions: The supplied summary describes temporal GRU gates and mechanisms for short- and longer-term interests.
limitations: Its richer memory mechanisms require additional implementation and attribution experiments.
It provides conceptual motivation rather than benchmark evidence for the proposed alternatives.
